# New Hampshire — the source registry

**GENERATED BY HAND AND MAINTAINED BY HAND. One row per source.** This is the
per-state half of the source registry, which stays the project-wide source of
record for what resources exist; this file answers the same questions for New
Hampshire specifically, at the granularity a hunt actually needs.

**Born 2026-08-26** (the sources-and-incumbency session, Item 2). The three
files in this folder do three different jobs and they stay separate on purpose:

- **`sources.md`** — this file. The registry. Structured, one row per source.
- **`NOTES.md`** — the internal dossier. Candid, never published. How this state
  actually works, where we stand in it, what has already bitten us. It predates
  this file (born 2026-08-15) and **the repo's naming wins over the brief's**:
  there is no `dossier.md` here, and creating one beside `NOTES.md` would leave
  two files claiming the same job.
- **`explainer.md`** — reader-facing, plain language, **NOT PUBLISHED YET**.

**Every entry carries: name, URL, publisher, classification, licence, access,
what it carries, coverage, freshness, the primaries it points to, and whether we
use it. An entry missing any of those is INCOMPLETE and says so.**

**Classification** (RULING 87's distinction, generalised):

- **PRIMARY** — the body that holds the office or the record publishes it.
- **DERIVED-POINTER** — a third party that names where the primary is. Followed
  down; never cited.
- **DERIVED-CONTENT** — a third party that republishes or rewrites the content.
  Never ingested.

**Tier** is RULING 84's, as amended by **RULING 166**: **A0** the body's own
publication and the tier above it in government; **A1** third-party compilations
answering many entities at once; **B** the entity's own official source, per
entity; **C** per-entity search.

**Licence is QUOTED with its URL, or reads NONE STATED.** It is never inferred
and never assumed permissive.

**`EmployeeNo` joins a legislator to every one of their roll calls with no name

**The address correction, recorded rather than smoothed.** The brief that

## The Secretary of State — walked as a BODY, division by division

**PERMISSION ANSWERED 2026-08-31 (Session C). The 403 was our own name.**

What stood here until then: *every division below answers HTTP 403 to both a
plain client and a full browser header set, including `robots.txt` itself* —
which made the permission question **UNANSWERED**, and under RULING 148 an
unanswered permission question refuses the walk. That refusal is why this whole
fact class sat unwalked, and the wall was never re-tested at a higher rung.

It was our identification, not us:

- **`https://www.sos.nh.gov/robots.txt` answers HTTP 200 to a bare client** —
  2103 bytes, a standard Drupal file — **and 403 to the identical request whose
  User-Agent carries this project's name.** That is the
  `identified-agent-refused` route (measured across the `nh.gov` family on
  2026-08-26) applied to the permission read itself. Every `Disallow` in it is a
  CMS internal: `/core/`, `/profiles/`, `/admin/`, `/user/login`, `/search/`,
  the README files. **Nothing disallows elections, campaign finance, or the
  lobbyist registry.**
- **`cfs.sos.nh.gov` publishes no `robots.txt` at all.** It returns its Angular
  shell for `/robots.txt` byte-identically to what it returns for a nonsense
  path. That is an **absence of published restrictions**, recorded as exactly
  that — never as a 200 that grants permission, because a SPA catch-all is not a
  rule.

So the walk is permitted, and identification now travels in `From:` and
`X-Purpose:` headers, which this host serves, rather than in a User-Agent it
refuses. **The rungs below are therefore superseded as a permission finding;
they remain accurate as a record of what an identified client was served.**

**And the route is a script, not a procedure.** The rung-7 route recorded on
2026-08-21 called the API "from the page's own origin" because a browser is
bound by CORS. A server is not. `pnpm money:nh` now reads
`cfsapi.sos.nh.gov/api/PublicFilerDetails/GetFilingEntityDetails` with a plain
POST, no browser and no session — which is what tracker row **NH40** said could
not be done. Both findings are in the method store as
`unanswered-permission-may-be-the-agent-not-the-host` and
`ask-what-the-browser-was-for-before-recording-human-only`.

| Division | URL | Classification | Status, tested 2026-08-26 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lobbyist registry** | `https://www.sos.nh.gov/lobbyists` | PRIMARY | **HTTP 403** at rungs 2 and 3. **A source class this product holds NOTHING of, in any state except Arizona** |
| **Campaign finance system** | `https://cfs.sos.nh.gov/public/cf/downloads` | PRIMARY | **HTTP 403** at rungs 2 and 3 |
| **CFS reports** | `https://cfs.sos.nh.gov/public/cf/reports` | PRIMARY | not separately walked; same host, same wall |
| **CFS contributions** | `https://cfs.sos.nh.gov/public/cf/contribution` | PRIMARY | not separately walked; same host, same wall |
| **CFS login** | `https://cfs.sos.nh.gov/login` | — | **NOT WALKED AND NEVER WILL BE.** A login page is an access control. Recorded so the next session does not spend a rung on it |
| **Elections / candidate filings** | `https://www.sos.nh.gov/elections/...` | PRIMARY | 403 host-wide today. the source registry records a 2.95 MB HTTP 200 on 2026-08-24, so **this wall is intermittent**, which is itself the finding |

**Licence for all of the above:** NONE STATED — no terms document was reached,
because the host was not reached. **Recorded as unread rather than as
permissive.**

**The receipts file key, recorded as a FINDING and not a footnote.** The brief
records that NH's published campaign-finance file key documents a
**candidate-name-as-it-appears-on-the-ballot** field, distinct from the legal
name. **This session could not confirm it — the host refused at every rung
walked** — so it is carried here as an unconfirmed lead with its origin named,
never as a fact. If it holds, it is direct evidence for the class of defect
behind the incumbency work: a candidate's filed name and their serving name
differ, and any join on a name string breaks on exactly that.

**The disagreement, stated as a pair (RULING 147 — this is an EXTERNAL anchor,
two publications about the same 2026 legislature):**

| | Rows |
|---|---|
| `gc.nh.gov/downloads/Members.txt`, read 2026-08-26 | **408** (384 House, 24 Senate) |
| LegiScan NH dataset, `peopleSeen`, snapshot 2026-08-26 | **426** |

**They disagree by 18, and 18 is exactly the number of rows `Members.txt` marks
`Former`.** That is a reconciliation, not a coincidence, and it is recorded as
one: the two publications are counting different populations at different
moments, and neither is wrong. **What IS a finding is the third number:
LegiScan's NH `peopleMatched` is 85.** So 341 of 426 New Hampshire legislators'
roll calls sit in a committed snapshot in this repository and reach no reader,
because the join to our officeholder records fails. See the incumbency work in
the same session's report.

## What is NOT here, said plainly

- **No lobbyist data.** The registry exists at `sos.nh.gov/lobbyists` and
  refused every rung walked on 2026-08-26.
- **No state campaign-finance data.** Same host family, same refusal.
- **No municipal clerk directory for New Hampshire.** Citizens Count points at
  one held by the Secretary of State; the Secretary of State is walled. This is
  a NAMED gap with its branches and its date, not an absence.
- **No `dynamicdatadump` parse.** The endpoint answers; nobody has read it.

## Freshness cadence

Under **RULING 96** and **RULING 53**: candidate fields 7 days, bodies and
rosters 14 days, walled sources 14 days. Every row above carries the date it was
last walked. A row past its window is **STALE** and is re-walked before it is
relied on. Re-walk with `pnpm robots:sweep` for the permission question and the
per-source route for the content.

## THE DESCENT — every level walked, and its counts (RULING 169)

**Walked 2026-08-26** by `pnpm descent --state nh`, 2 pass(es).
The full walk is `states/nh/descent.md`; every candidate it named is
`states/nh/descent-candidates.md`. This section is the REGISTER entry for it.

| Tier | Found | Followed | Yielded | Barren | Declined | Candidates NEW | Candidates known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | 2 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | **53** | 0 |
| `multi-county` | 55 | 33 | 13 | 20 | 22 | **105** | 20 |
| `special-district` | 26 | 26 | 19 | 7 | 0 | **61** | 0 |
| `minor-civil` | 8 | 6 | 1 | 5 | 2 | **9** | 0 |
| `county` | 8 | 8 | 3 | 5 | 0 | **9** | 2 |

**99 links found · 75 followed · 237 CANDIDATE bodies not already matched in the registry.**

**THE WALK STOPPED, IT DID NOT FINISH.** Pass 2 queued
**771** link(s) that were never followed. RULING 169: if the final pass found
anything new, the walk was not finished and the session says so. Those links are the next
session's resume point, and they are held in the frontier the run rebuilt rather than in a list
anybody has to remember.

**They are CANDIDATES and not bodies.** A candidate is a link whose text named a governing body;
confirming it, resolving it to a division and giving it an id is the next motion. Reporting the
number as *bodies discovered* would be a claim about coverage this product does not have.

**Freshness: last walked 2026-08-26.** RULING 96 — a source past expiry is re-walked or
reported STALE with its date. Bodies and rosters carry a 14-day clock (RULING 53).
